title: The photos from Saturday
setting: Monday lunch break at the office. On Saturday, Yuki, her coworker Mai and Yuki's old friend Kenta spent a sunny day out together, and both women took lots of photos on their phones. Yuki is still waiting for Mai to send hers.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: nee, mai. doyoubi no shashin, okutte kurenai?
lines.ja: ねえ、マイ。土曜日の写真、送ってくれない？
lines.kana: ねえ、まい。どようびのしゃしん、おくってくれない？
lines.english: Hey, Mai. Could you send me the photos from Saturday?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ii yo. demo, chotto kono shashin mite.
lines.ja: いいよ。でも、ちょっとこの写真見て。
lines.kana: いいよ。でも、ちょっとこのしゃしんみて。
lines.english: Sure. But take a look at this photo.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: nani? are? kore, watashi? sumaho ijitteru.
lines.ja: 何？あれ？これ、私？スマホいじってる。
lines.kana: なに？あれ？これ、わたし？スマホいじってる。
lines.english: What? Huh? Is that me? I'm on my phone.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kore mo, kore mo. tenki yokatta noni, yuki, zutto sumaho ijitteta yo.
lines.ja: これも、これも。天気よかったのに、ユキ、ずっとスマホいじってたよ。
lines.kana: これも、これも。てんきよかったのに、ゆき、ずっとスマホいじってたよ。
lines.english: This one too, and this one. The weather was so nice, and you were on your phone the whole time.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: demo, ijitteta wake ja nai yo. jibun de totta shashin, miteta n da yo.
lines.ja: でも、いじってたわけじゃないよ。自分で撮った写真、見てたんだよ。
lines.kana: でも、いじってたわけじゃないよ。じぶんでとったしゃしん、みてたんだよ。
lines.english: But I wasn't just messing about on it. I was looking at the photos I'd taken.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sore o sumaho ijitteru tte iu no.
lines.ja: それをスマホいじってるって言うの。
lines.kana: それをスマホいじってるっていうの。
lines.english: That's what being on your phone means.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, watashi ga totta shashin mo mite yo.
lines.ja: じゃあ、私が撮った写真も見てよ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、わたしがとったしゃしんもみてよ。
lines.english: Okay, then look at the photos I took, too.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, kore, watashi? ki ga tsukanakatta.
lines.ja: え、これ、私？気がつかなかった。
lines.kana: え、これ、わたし？きがつかなかった。
lines.english: Huh, is that me? I didn't even notice you taking it.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ne? mai mo zutto ijitteta yo.
lines.ja: ね？マイもずっといじってたよ。
lines.kana: ね？まいもずっといじってたよ。
lines.english: See? You were on yours the whole time too.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: watashi wa, uchi no neko no shashin miteta no.
lines.ja: 私は、うちの猫の写真見てたの。
lines.kana: わたしは、うちのねこのしゃしんみてたの。
lines.english: I was looking at photos of my cat.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sore o sumaho ijitteru tte iu n da yo.
lines.ja: それをスマホいじってるって言うんだよ。
lines.kana: それをスマホいじってるっていうんだよ。
lines.english: That's what being on your phone means, you know.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: tashika ni. jaa, kondo wa minna de shashin torou.
lines.ja: 確かに。じゃあ、今度はみんなで写真撮ろう。
lines.kana: たしかに。じゃあ、こんどはみんなでしゃしんとろう。
lines.english: Fair point. Next time, let's take a photo of all of us together.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un. a, demo kono shashin, kenta ni wa okuranaide ne.
lines.ja: うん。あ、でもこの写真、ケンタには送らないでね。
lines.kana: うん。あ、でもこのしゃしん、けんたにはおくらないでね。
lines.english: Yeah. Oh, but don't send these photos to Kenta, okay?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, gomen. kenta-kun ni wa, kesa okutchatta.
lines.ja: あ、ごめん。ケンタくんには、今朝送っちゃった。
lines.kana: あ、ごめん。けんたくんには、けさおくっちゃった。
lines.english: Oh, sorry. I sent them to Kenta this morning.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e! watashi ni wa mada shashin okutte kuretenai noni!
lines.ja: え！私にはまだ写真送ってくれてないのに！
lines.kana: え！わたしにはまだしゃしんおくってくれてないのに！
lines.english: What? You still haven't even sent me the photos!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: de, kenta-kun kara, futari tomo, zutto sumaho ijitteta ne tte kita.
lines.ja: で、ケンタくんから「二人とも、ずっとスマホいじってたね」って来た。
lines.kana: で、けんたくんから「ふたりとも、ずっとスマホいじってたね」ってきた。
lines.english: And Kenta wrote back: "You two were on your phones the whole time, huh."

choices.english: Yuki wants Saturday's photos to send to Kenta, but Mai was on her phone all day and didn't take any.
Each of them has photos of the other on her phone all day, and Mai has already sent hers to Kenta.
Mai is upset that Yuki took photos of her without asking, so Yuki promises not to send them to Kenta.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Yuki asks Mai to send the Saturday photos. Lines 2-4: Mai's photos show Yuki on her phone the whole day (zutto sumaho ijitteta). Lines 7-10: Yuki's photos show Mai on hers too, looking at pictures of her cat. Line 14: Mai sent her photos to Kenta this morning, before she sent them to Yuki, and in line 16 Kenta writes back teasing them both. A is wrong because Mai did take photos (she shows them in line 2), and it's Yuki who doesn't want them sent to Kenta (line 13). C is wrong because Mai only says she didn't notice the photo being taken (line 8); she isn't upset, and the photos Yuki doesn't want sent are Mai's photos of her.

questions.english: You're out for a walk with Kenta when he stops and says: "Look! This place is amazing." Ask him to take a photo of you here.
questions.answer: Ask for a photo with shashin (o) toru in the te-form request: koko de shashin totte! or the softer shashin totte moraeru?

modelAnswers.ja: ねえ、ここで写真撮って！
modelAnswers.english: Hey, take a picture of me here!

modelAnswers.ja: ほんとだ。写真撮ってもらえる？
modelAnswers.english: You're right. Could you take a picture of me?

questions.explanation: For photos, English 'take' really is toru: Mai says kondo wa minna de shashin torou (line 12), and Yuki talks about the photos she took, jibun de totta shashin (line 5) and watashi ga totta shashin (line 7). It's the one 'take' that works this way: medicine is kusuri o nomu and a train is densha ni noru. Don't say shashin o morau: that means getting a photo from someone. To ask, use the te-form (shashin totte) or -te moraeru? to sound softer.

questions.english: Mai says Yuki was on her phone the whole time. What does Yuki say she was actually doing on it?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、スマホで何をしていましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、スマホでなにをしていましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, sumaho de nani o shite imashita ka?

choices.english: Looking at the photos she had taken.

questions.explanation: Line 5: jibun de totta shashin, miteta n da yo. miteta is shashin o miru, looking at photos. totta only says which photos: the ones she had taken herself. B mixes up the two verbs. A is okuru, which comes up later, when Mai says she has already sent her photos to Kenta (line 14). Mai's comeback in line 6 is that looking at photos on your phone all day still counts as sumaho o ijiru, and she then makes the same excuse herself in line 10 (neko no shashin miteta no).

questions.english: When Mai shows Yuki the photos, what does she say Yuki was doing all day?
questions.ja: マイさんは、土曜日のユキさんについて、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、どようびのゆきさんについて、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, doyoubi no yuki-san ni tsuite, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: You were on your phone the whole time.
You were using your phone the whole time.
You were playing on your phone the whole time.

questions.explanation: Line 4: tenki yokatta noni, yuki, zutto sumaho ijitteta yo. Being idly on your phone is sumaho (o) ijiru, and about someone else it carries a mild complaint, as it does here. Mai says it again in line 6 and Kenta does in line 16. B, tsukau, is 'use' word for word. It would be understood, but it sounds like using the phone for a task, such as a call or a map. C, sumaho de asobu, means playing games on it, and nobody was doing that: Yuki was looking at her photos and Mai at photos of her cat.

questions.english: Mai tells you: "Some of yesterday's photos came out really well." Ask her to send them to you.
questions.ja: 昨日の写真、すごくいいのあるよ。
questions.kana: きのうのしゃしん、すごくいいのあるよ。
questions.romaji: kinou no shashin, sugoku ii no aru yo.
questions.answer: Ask with okuru as a request: shashin okutte, or okutte kurenai? to be softer. The person you send to takes ni: watashi ni mo okutte.

modelAnswers.ja: ほんと？じゃあ、その写真送って！
modelAnswers.english: Really? Then send them to me!

modelAnswers.romaji: sugoi! watashi ni mo shashin okutte kurenai?
modelAnswers.ja: すごい！私にも写真送ってくれない？
modelAnswers.english: Nice! Could you send me the photos too?

questions.explanation: Yuki asks the same way in line 1 (doyoubi no shashin, okutte kurenai?) and complains in line 15 (watashi ni wa mada shashin okutte kuretenai noni!). The person takes ni: kenta ni wa okuranaide (line 13), kenta-kun ni wa okutchatta (line 14). shashin misete would only ask her to show them to you on her phone, the way Mai holds hers out in line 2 (kono shashin mite). okutte gets them onto your own phone. When photos or replies arrive, the verb is kuru: Kenta's reply in line 16 ends tte kita.

newWords.english: two people (futari tomo = both of you)
friendly name suffix, mostly for young men (kenta-kun)
